summary: Reverified the reviewed header implementation (a8641026, unchanged src/ui/header.rs) for this execution: the F19 title/status divider and the concentric status-dot ring with its state animations still pass the scoped loop and the full gate, with no source changes.

HEADER-TITLE-DIVIDER-AND-STATUS-RING.evidence: Re-executed on the unchanged implementation: the header paints the reference's 1x16 slate-200 divider between the title and the status line (the_title_and_status_are_separated_by_the_reference_divider), and the status dot paints its 8px circle inside the 4px ring in the reference's four state pairs with the amber measuring pulse and the indigo rebinding ping (the_synced_dot_wears_the_emerald_ring, the_idle_dot_stays_slate_without_an_animation, the_measuring_dot_pulses_amber, the_rebinding_dot_pings_indigo, the_pulse_and_ping_waves_match_the_reference_cycles, the_dot_state_follows_the_reference_precedence), with the unowned ui_semantic rebinding flow passing against the animated dot in this execution's egui-ui run.

risks: The ring steps amber-100 (#fef3c6) and emerald-100 (#d0fae5) and the indigo-500 ink (#615fff) are derived from the reference's Tailwind v4 oklch declarations; the conversion reproduces five verified theme read-backs exactly, but theme.rs owns no such tokens and is outside this task's ownership (preview.rs carries the same indigo-500 for its dot highlight).

The dot requests its next frame at the backend's predicted frame time plus a millisecond rather than a fixed 60 Hz delay, because egui subtracts the predicted frame time from every request and a smaller delay collapses into an immediate repaint loop; the animation therefore follows the backend cadence.

The inactive state folds the disconnected runtime into the reference's engine-off slate pair, because the reference has no separate connection state and no engine status can be trusted without a connection.
Native visual confirmation is outside this execution; the divider, ring, and animations are pinned by egui_kittest widget and unit tests only.
